result:
Two findings, two outcomes.

**Minor (typo):** I fix it. It is a docstring change with no behavior to test, so there is no RED step, and `make test` is the gate.

**Important (switch to ROUND_HALF_UP):** I do not apply it. The finding contradicts D2, an owner decision from plan review: "prices round half-even (ROUND_HALF_EVEN), to match the ledger system." The reviewer's reason is "customers expect half-up", with no evidence and no spec reference. D2 is a decision, not a scope fence, and none of the five stops applies, so I rule instead of stalling. The ruling is ledgered and the partner sees it at the plan-completion gate.

<edit path="rates/card.py">
    '''Round a price to whole cents. A tie goes to the nearest even cent.'''
</edit>

<edit path=".sdd/14-rate-card/progress.md">
Final review: Ruling: declined reviewer finding "switch round_price() to ROUND_HALF_UP"; kept ROUND_HALF_EVEN — plan Decision D2 (owner, 2026-11-02) requires half-even to match the ledger system, and the reviewer cited no spec basis for half-up — if wrong, tie prices (e.g. 0.125) round one cent lower than customers expect and diverge from the ledger system only if D2 itself is revisited; the change is a one-line constant swap plus the affected test expectations.
Final review: fixed Minor — "neerest" → "nearest" in round_price() docstring (no behavior change, no RED test applicable).
</edit>

<command>
make test > .sdd/14-rate-card/final-fix-test.log 2>&1; tail -n 15 .sdd/14-rate-card/final-fix-test.log
</command>

If the tail shows the suite passing, I commit and the ledger lines go in with it:

<command>
git add rates/card.py && git commit -m "fix: correct typo in round_price docstring" && git rev-parse --short HEAD
</command>

If `make test` fails, I do not commit. I debug first, though a docstring change should not break anything. After the commit, the plan-completion protocol and finishing-a-development-branch follow.

**Message to partner (at the plan-completion gate):**

> All tasks in `specs/plans/14-rate-card.md` are complete and `make test` passes. The whole-plan review returned two findings:
>
> 1. **Fixed:** the docstring typo "neerest" in `round_price()`.
> 2. **Declined, your call if you disagree:** the reviewer asked to switch `round_price()` to ROUND_HALF_UP because "customers expect half-up". That contradicts D2 (your 2026-11-02 decision: half-even, to match the ledger system), and the reviewer gave no spec basis. I kept ROUND_HALF_EVEN and ledgered it as a ruling in `.sdd/14-rate-card/progress.md`.
>
> If you want half-up, it is a one-line change in `rates/card.py` plus the tie-case test expectations, and D2 would need updating. If customer-facing prices should differ from the ledger system, it is worth deciding that explicitly.
